statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F(x,y,z) = x\vec j + y\vec k through the surface S, where S is the part of the surface z=-y+1 above the rectangle 0\le x\le 4, 0\le y\le 1, oriented upward.

static.solution: S as z=f(x,y)=-y + 1, we have d\vec A= (-f_x\vec i - f_y\vec j + \vec k)dxdy = \vec j + \vec k. Thus, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{1}\int_0^{4} ( x\vec j + y\vec k)\cdot (\vec j+\vec k)\,dxdy = \int_0^{1}\int_0^{4} x + y\, dxdy = \int_0^{1} (\frac{1}{2} x^2 + xy)\bigg|_0^{4}\,dy = \int_0^{1} (8 + 4 y)\,dy = (8 y + 2 y^2)\bigg|_0^{1}= 10.
